lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Barbara, Beth here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the bedtime goal went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You can't be eating at 10 at night.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is coffee with milk the first thing you have?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, no, not really. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, we had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Family time comes first, and food is a big part of that.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to finish eating by 7:30 on 3 nights next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 7. Maybe 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stop eating at 8, I just need tea at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the parties gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, if it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Barbara. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Reports partial progress on bedtime goal
Directive opening; participant only says Okay
Overstates commitment; participant was still ambivalent
Filler acknowledgement, no reflection of content
Reasons: blood sugar, family history fears
Validates sustain talk without exploring ambivalence
Fear-based warning after information without consent
Says yes, then returns to party barrier
Sets goal for her without collaboration
Identifies feasible plan: tea at night

flags.reason: Opens with directive 'You can't be eating at 10 at night' before exploring participant's view.
Fear-based warning about health suffering; pushes without permission and after participant had only shown openness.
Argues 'research is very clear' right after participant's change talk; repeated persuading pattern with 38.
Imperative 'You have to make this a priority' increases resistance; participant responds defensively at 39.
Sets a specific goal ('Let's put you down') without collaborative negotiation; participant only says Maybe.
Reflects sustain talk about family food without eliciting ambivalence or change talk from participant's own reasons.

score.summary: Coach used frequent directives and warnings (lines 5, 30, 36, 38, 40) that met resistance, though the participant still produced clear change talk about her alarm, fridge reminder, and fear of recurrence. Strong closing: the coach elicited a self-generated backup plan (line 46) and a confidence rating (line 42), and the participant's final commitments came from her own ideas.
strengths: Line 7 and 50: affirmed the participant's effort and starting the process.
Line 18: complex reflection captured the participant's ambivalence ('Part of you is already moving').
Line 26: asked permission before sharing information (line 28).
Line 44 and 46: open questions drew out her reasons for confidence and a backup plan.
coaching_tips: Replace line 5 and 36 persuasion with an open question, e.g., 'What do you make of the evening eating pattern?'
Before line 30, ask permission and explore her own concerns about her father's diabetes rather than warning her.
At line 40, offer options and ask 'What feels doable to you next week?' to co-create the goal.
At line 21 and 35, use a complex reflection that explores both sides, e.g., 'Family food matters to you, and you also want your sugar better.'
Summarize the plan before closing (line 48) and check her feelings about the plan.
